Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

they pronoun

also them, those people

classical

Liv. 5.41.9: ad eōs velut simulācra versī
Cic. Att. 6.1.12: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur

eī (iī), eae, ea

pronoun: plural of is; genitive eōrum, eārum, dative and ablative eīs (iīs)

they, them

Mostly left out as subject: amant inter sē, exercentur, they love each other, they play. For “them” as object, eōs, eās, ea (ad eōs … versī). In reported speech, “they” meaning the speakers is sē.

Other words

  • illī, illae, illa — they, those people

    pronoun: plural of ille, declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.17.24; Cic. Fin. 5.61: ut illī efferuntur laetitiā, cum vīcērunt!

    For a group set against another, or a new subject: nec ipse meōrum lūsibus nec illī studiīs meīs obstrepunt.

  • hī, hae, haec — they, these people (here)

    pronoun: plural of hic · also used · classical

    The people present or just named.

  • eccōs, eccās — there they are!

    interjection with the accusative: ecce with eōs, eās · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 641: eccās

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Pointing them out; eccum, eccam for one.

Examples

  • Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus

    The boys Cicero love each other, they play together, but they learn too; one … needs the reins, the other the spurs.Cic. Att. 6.1.12

  • ad eōs velut simulācra versī cum stārent

    as they stood turned towards them as if towards statuesLiv. 5.41.9

  • nam nec ipse meōrum lūsibus nec illī studiīs meīs obstrepunt

    for I don’t disturb my household’s games, nor they my workPlin. Ep. 2.17.24

  • quanta studia dēcertantium sunt! quanta ipsa certāmina! ut illī efferuntur laetitiā, cum vīcērunt! ut pudet victōs! ut sē accūsārī nōlunt! quam cupiunt laudārī!

    How keen the competitors are! How fierce the contests themselves! How carried away with joy they are when they have won! How ashamed the losers! How they hate to be blamed! How they long to be praised!Cic. Fin. 5.61

  • Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.

    Show me your hands. — There you are, I’ve shown them: here they are.Plaut. Aul. 640b–641

See also he, their, themselves, each other.
